chunks: Ishaq ibn Ammar asked Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام:
About a man who frees his slave as a delayed emancipation and then becomes in need of his price. He said: "He may sell him."
He said: I said, "Then if he has no need of his price?" He said: "If the slave agrees, then there is no harm."

key_terms.عَنْ دُبُرٍ: as a delayed emancipation to take effect after death
key_terms.غِنًى: freedom from need or financial sufficiency
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or no objection

ai.seo_question: Can a mudabbar slave be sold if the owner later needs money?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a slave designated for emancipation after the owner's death. If the owner later needs the slave's monetary value, he may sell him; if there is no such need, the sale is permitted only with the slave's consent.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3456 - Ishaq ibn Ammar asked Abu Ibrahim (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim) (as), about a man who frees his slave as a delayed emancipation (to take effect after his death) and then becomes in need of the slave's price.

I asked: "What if he is not in need of the price?"
Imam (as) said: "If the slave agrees, then there is no harm."
